solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pay cut, story unrivalled

indicators.note: cut tells us to clip the last letter off the word for pay

parts.note: a parable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A worker complains that a pay cut is an unparalleled tale of woe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the final E from INCOME, leaving INCOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without rival is beyond comparison, matchless.

clue.text: Device that sprays blue rinse all over the place

indicators.note: letters scattered all over the place are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's spray gun spatters blue hair dye everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' rearranges BLUE RINSE. A blue rinse is a tint traditionally used on grey hair by older British women.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical gadget turns liquid medicine into a fine mist for inhaling.

clue.text: Canoe I manoeuvred over a Southern Hemisphere area

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first
letters manoeuvred are moved about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A paddler steers a canoe across some southern stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvred' rearranges CANOE I into OCEANI, which sits 'over' A in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The region takes in Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands, mostly south of the equator.

clue.text: He or she, perhaps, has to consolidate declaration

parts.note: he and she are examples of a part of speech standing in for a noun
to cement a bond is to consolidate it

explanation.surface: Someone must firm up an official statement, whoever they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks he or she as examples of a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal statement made publicly is a declaration.

clue.text: Jolly man? Got it!

definitions.meaning: the Jolly ... is the pirate flag, so the man's name follows Jolly
radio speak for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A cheerful fellow exclaims that he has understood.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag bears this name after Jolly, and radio operators say it to acknowledge a message.

clue.text: Grub's ending in waste receptacle

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Old food ends up thrown in the rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letter of Grub, B; grub is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A container for rubbish is a dustbin, shortened to its familiar form.

clue.text: Pass old germ orally?

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former or old

indicators.note: orally says the word is spoken, so we write what it sounds like

parts.note: a seed is the germ from which something grows

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an ancient bacterium can be passed on by mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond a limit is to overtake or surpass it.

clue.text: Exclusive southern home for chickens!

explanation.surface: A newspaper splashes a story about a southern henhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A news story that one paper gets ahead of rivals is an exclusive.

clue.text: First of criteria fit for message

indicators.note: First of takes the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: fit, as in capable, means able

explanation.surface: The top criterion is whether something is suitable to send as a message.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram was a message sent by telegraph wire, hence its other name.

clue.text: Natural bend on cigar

indicators.note: to bend letters is to twist them into another order

explanation.surface: A smoker notices a bend in a natural, untreated cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: Produce grown without artificial chemicals is described this way, as is anything from living matter.

clue.text: US city or territory, old

explanation.surface: A question about whether some American place is a city or an old territory.
explanation.definitionFit: This Florida city is home to Disney World.

clue.text: Plunder weapon

definitions.meaning: to plunder is to ransack or search through and steal
a long-barrelled firearm fired from the shoulder

explanation.surface: Loot and guns, a bandit's inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means ransack, rummaging through to steal; as a noun it is a shoulder-fired gun.

clue.text: A face isn't made to beguile

indicators.note: made here means formed or fashioned into something else, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A face isn't painted to charm people, a beautician insists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges the letters of A FACE ISN'T; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm and captivate someone is to hold them spellbound.

clue.text: Reports claiming poor nag is left to rot

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to report something is to state it

indicators.note: poor tells us the word nag is in a bad state and its letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Accounts allege that a sorry old horse has been abandoned to decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' makes GNA, the anagram of the clue's horse, and 'claiming' sets it within the verb for reports; 'Reports' is not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or a situation left still and unchanged goes stale and decays.

clue.text: Quite awful Los Angeles drink

indicators.note: something awful is in a mess, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A visitor complains about a fairly dreadful drink served in Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: This Mexican spirit distilled from agave is a strong drink.

clue.text: Leader of clan in tartan, serene

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the other
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan chief stands calm in his tartan.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and untroubled, like still water, is a synonym for serene.

clue.text: Old king, brave man heading for defeat

parts.note: a hero is a brave man

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch, a courageous man, is heading towards defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' looks like 'going towards', but it takes D, the first letter of defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical ruler of Judea at the time of Jesus's birth is an old king.

clue.text: Part of Sicily, richly expressive

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A travel writer describes a part of Sicily in lush, emotive prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry that expresses the writer's feelings, songlike and emotional, is called this.

clue.text: Law works

definitions.meaning: a church rule or general principle
the accepted body of an author's writings

explanation.surface: Legal practice and output.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a church decree or rule, and also the collected writings regarded as genuine or important.

clue.text: Title say removed from essay and paper

indicators.note: removed from says the second word is taken out of the first

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: An editor strikes a word from an essay and the paper it is written on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes SAY out of ESSAY, leaving ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esq. is a courtesy title written after a man's name, especially in British letters.

clue.text: Rod contains desire for hot stuff

indicators.note: contains means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A rod packed with longing is something steamy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot stuff' suggests something sexy, but here it means a fiery spice.
explanation.definitionFit: This red pepper is ground into a fiery spice, so it is literally hot.

clue.text: Root vegetable taking a month to come up

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

explanation.surface: A gardener's root crop takes a month to sprout.
explanation.definitionFit: This starchy tuber is a staple crop eaten in Africa and the Caribbean.

clue.text: US state where I had a house

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the American state where they once owned a home.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-western state is famous for its potatoes.

clue.text: Devil started a bit differently, it's shown

indicators.note: letters arranged a bit differently are slightly rearranged

explanation.surface: A devil began his work in a new way, and it shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit differently' rearranges STARTED into STRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something proved or displayed openly has been made evident.
